Uber — peer benchmark

UBER-peer-benchmark-2026-10-14 · USD · series 2026-10-14T02:30:00Z · built 2026-10-14 15:26 UTC

The short version

Riders and eaters pay Uber to get a car or a meal to their door, and merchants and drivers pay it to reach them. Lyft, DoorDash and Grab do the same two jobs, rides and delivery, in different places and in different mixes, so this page puts each Uber business beside the rival that does that same job. Lyft is a rides-only business, mostly in the US, so its company figures sit beside Uber Mobility. DoorDash is delivery only, mostly in the US, so its company figures sit beside Uber Delivery. Grab runs both in Southeast Asia and prints each as its own segment. Every company counts bookings in its own way: Uber says Gross Bookings, Lyft says Gross Bookings, DoorDash says Marketplace GOV and Grab says GMV. Each chart labels them separately and does not convert one into another.

Mobility: Uber Mobility vs Lyft vs Grab Mobility

Delivery: Uber Delivery vs DoorDash vs Grab Deliveries

Where they operate

Lyft is mostly in the US and Canada, with a small European business since it bought Freenow. DoorDash is mostly in the US, and Wolt and Deliveroo carry it into Europe. Grab operates only in Southeast Asia, where Uber is not a direct rival. Uber reports revenue by region but does not split Mobility or Delivery by region.

Whole-company comparison

Operating income is the profit line every company reports. Margin is that profit divided by the company's own revenue.

Lyft's multiple is blank today because it never reports fourth-quarter EPS, so there are never four quarters to add up. Its roughly 2× in early 2026 came from a one-time tax benefit in its 2025 earnings, not from operating profit.

Key metrics

MetricTrendLine
Mobility scaleFar largerIn Q2 2026, Uber Mobility Gross Bookings were $29.0B, against Lyft's $5.5B and Grab Mobility GMV of $2.2B.
Mobility profitLarger, on a different lineIn Q2 2026, Uber Mobility segment operating income was $2.2B. Lyft's company Adjusted EBITDA was $177M and Grab Mobility segment Adjusted EBITDA was $191M.
Delivery scaleBehind DoorDashIn Q2 2026, Uber Delivery Gross Bookings were $27.5B, against DoorDash Marketplace GOV of $33.1B and Grab Deliveries GMV of $4.2B.
Delivery profitAhead, on a different lineIn Q2 2026, Uber Delivery segment operating income was $1.06B. DoorDash company Adjusted EBITDA was $914M and Grab Deliveries segment Adjusted EBITDA was $96M.
US exposureMost diversifiedIn 2025, 46% of Uber's revenue came from the US, against 96% for Lyft and 84% for DoorDash. Grab has no US revenue.
Operating marginHighest in the setIn Q2 2026, Uber's margin was 13.3%, against 3.5% for DoorDash and 2.6% for Lyft.
Trailing multiple (2026-W41)Lowest with a figureUber is at 15.4×, Grab 52× and DoorDash 101×. Lyft is blank because it doesn't report fourth-quarter EPS.

Open gaps

  • Uber does not split Mobility or Delivery by region. Only its total revenue is split by region.
  • From 2026, Uber reports segment operating income instead of segment Adjusted EBITDA, so the Adjusted EBITDA bars stop at Q4 2025. The operating-income bars start at Q4 2024, the earliest quarter Uber restated. Q3 2025 stays blank until Uber's Q3 2026 release restates it.
  • Lyft has no delivery business and DoorDash has no rides business. Their whole-company bookings, revenue and Adjusted EBITDA stand in for a segment and are labeled that way.
  • Uber's Trips count rides and delivery orders together, so Uber has no rides-only or delivery-only count. Grab reports only growth rates, not trip or order counts.
  • Lyft's Gross Bookings and Rides start in Q1 2022 (first printed as quarterly columns in the Q3 2023 release). Lyft Adjusted EBITDA is printed from Q1 2019 on the pre-2023 definition and from Q4 2021 on the current definition; the two series are not spliced. DoorDash's Marketplace GOV and Total Orders are blank for Q2 and Q3 2020. Uber's segment revenue is blank for Q4 2018.
  • Grab Mobility and Deliveries segment Adjusted EBITDA now include Q4 2020 prior-year prints from the Q4 2021 6-K; Deliveries GMV, revenue and segment Adjusted EBITDA also include Q1 2021 from the Q1 2022 6-K. Earlier pre-listing quarters stay blank.
  • Lyft's US share starts in 2023, the first year its annual report splits revenue between the US and elsewhere.
  • Lyft's fourth-quarter diluted EPS and share counts are blank. Neither its annual report nor its fourth-quarter earnings release reports a three-month per-share line, and we don't take the full year minus nine months.
  • Grab's diluted share counts for the first three quarters of 2021 are blank, and quarters before each company listed are blank.
  • Weekly multiples are blank wherever trailing earnings were a loss. Year-over-year growth is blank wherever the prior period was a loss or the sign flipped.
  • Forward multiples are empty for every company.
